newsitem.title: UK: Russian Urals done at Dtd - 80 cts pre Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Russian Urals done at Dtd - 80 cts pre Iraq news.

text.p: Two cargoes of Russian Urals sour changed hands at Dated Brent -80 cents on Tuesday and most traders assessed the grade little changed on Wednesday despite bearish news suggesting an early resumption of Iraqi exports.

The million barrel cargoes loading July 14-15 and July 16-17 moved at the firm number in the morning, before Iraq announced in the afternoon that it hoped to resume oil exports in a week to 10 days' time.
A third cargo of 80,000 tonnes was also heard changing hands at about Dated -80 cents on Tuesday morning, but few details were available.
Traders said the firmness of the Russian grade, the main regional competitor for Iraqi Kirkuk, was due in large part to the scarcity of Urals in the near-term and the continuing absence of Kirkuk.

But most traders added they saw the Urals market continuing at around these levels on Wednesday because they were sceptical about the possibility that Iraq would be in a position to resume sales by early July.
They said that among other things no lifter had as yet signed contracts.
They noted Baghdad and the United Nations still needed to solve a number of issues related to the launch of the second 180-day period of the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme.
Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in Vienna on Tuesday his country would start exporting oil again once the "oil-for-food" aid distribution plan had been finalised in seven to 10 days.
